issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Pneumatic.openValve(): The UML in the problem statement (Pneumatic.openValve()) declares a no-argument method 'openValve()'. In solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java the interface declares 'void openValve(int duration);' (one int parameter). However, the solution classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement a no-argument 'public void openValve()' method. This inconsistency (interface declares a parameter but implementations and UML declare none) will cause compilation errors and leaves students unclear which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface signature consistent with the UML and the implementing classes by changing the interface method to 'void openValve();'. Alternatively, if an int duration parameter was intended, update the problem statement UML and change both implementing classes to implement 'public void openValve(int duration)' and update any tests/documentation accordingly. Prefer the first option to match the given UML.

issues.description: The Pneumatic.openValve operation is described in the problem UML and remarks as a no-argument method named openValve(). In the solution repository, the Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration) (an int-parameter version), while the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement a no-argument openValve() method. This creates a naming/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (openValve) across artifacts and will confuse students and cause compilation/signature errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare void openValve() (no parameters) to match the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes, and ensure all implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) use the same no-argument signature. If a duration parameter is required, instead update the problem statement UML and all implementations to consistently use openValve(int duration).
